findings.claim: Replacing a provider store abandons the previous RealtimeManager without clearing any queued realtime flush, so a pending timer can still write into the old graph after adapter cleanup.
findings.evidence: The hook creates a new `RealtimeManager` whenever `[store, options.flushInterval]` changes, but returns only the manager and no cleanup/dispose path; `packages/entity-graph-core/src/adapters/realtime-manager.ts` keeps `pendingChanges` and `flushTimer` as private state, while `examples/nextjs-app/src/demo-pages/realtime/realtime-page.tsx` cleanup only calls `adapter.stop()` and `unregister()`.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `dispose()`/`clearPending()` method to `RealtimeManager` that clears `flushTimer`, pending queues, and registered adapters, and call it from the hook/effect cleanup when the scoped manager is replaced or unmounted.
